headline: One-time charges mask underlying strength; guidance raised
summary_short: Ford posted Q2 FY2026 revenue of $48.3B (down 4% y/y) and a GAAP net loss of $1.3B, driven mainly by a $3.6B non-cash charge tied to the BlueOval SK joint-venture disposition; adjusted EBIT rose to $2.5B (+$0.4B y/y) and the company raised full-year adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.0-11.0B.
summary_long: Revenue fell to $48.3B (-4% y/y) on lower wholesale volumes (1,039k units, -12% y/y) from product discontinuations, aluminum supply constraints, and Gen-1 EV right-sizing, partly offset by favorable mix. GAAP net loss of $1.3B reflects $4.2B of pre-tax special items, primarily a $3.6B largely non-cash charge from the BlueOval SK joint-venture disposition and $0.5B from EV program cancellations. Adjusted EBIT rose to $2.5B (+$0.4B y/y): Ford Pro EBIT fell to $1.7B on aluminum constraints, Ford Blue EBIT rose to $1.1B, and Model e's loss narrowed to $919M. Operating cash flow was $4.3B; cash and liquidity stood at $22.3B and $43.4B. Ford raised FY2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.0-11.0B and adjusted FCF guidance to $6.0-7.0B, and declared a 15-cent Q3 dividend.
